text:
Jordan: heads up — customer acme-tools is hitting a burst of 429s on paginated GETs to /v1/objects?cursor=... They say their client retries and then the account gets pegged; logs show repeated request ids and the same page refetched multiple times. No obvious 5xx in the window, mostly 429s.

OpsBot: automated alert: rate-limit breach detected for account=acme-tools bucket=read-pool usage=88% threshold=80% ts=2026-03-13T03:12:30Z

Maya: can you paste the minimal repro + which client version they're using? Are they using our SDK auto-pagination or a custom loop? Any idempotency header being set?

Jordan: they are on js-sdk v2.1.0, using the SDK's built-in pager with concurrency=4. When a page hits 429, the SDK retries the individual GET and doesn't coordinate across the pager, so multiple concurrent pages will retry in parallel and amplify the burst. Example log snippet from their side: 
```
[2026-03-13T03:12:45Z] request id=abc123 route=/v1/objects?cursor=ey... status=429 attempt=1
[2026-03-13T03:12:46Z] request id=abc123 status=429 attempt=2
[2026-03-13T03:12:47Z] request id=def456 route=/v1/objects?cursor=ey... status=429 attempt=1
```
They also show the SDK configured with retries=5 and no special handling for 429 Retry-After.

Liam (SDK): thanks — quick note on defaults: js-sdk v2.x uses up to 4 retries by default with exponential backoff (base ~200ms, cap ~10s) and full jitter. Historically the SDK retried on network errors and 5xx; we added 429 to the retry set but didn't coordinate across pagers. Important: GETs are idempotent, so retries are allowed, but they can still amplify a quota-limited resource if many concurrent requests fail and retry at similar cadence.

Liam (SDK): actionable fixes from SDK side we can consider:
- implement per-pager backoff coordination (single page failure pauses other page fetches for a short jittered backoff)
- honor server Retry-After header strictly for 429 (currently we backoff but don't always use server-provided Retry-After)
- expose a "no-auto-retry" flag on the pager so customers can implement their own page-level retry logic

Jen (SRE): additional system-level notes: always advise customers to check our rate headers: X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining / X-RateLimit-Reset and the Retry-After header. If Retry-After is present, clients must defer further attempts until after the indicated window. If the client ignores Retry-After and retries aggressively, it will cause sustained quota exhaustion and billing spikes. Also: our read pool has a burst bucket to allow short spikes; the behavior you see is consistent with a thundering-herd of retries after transient throttles.

Maya: recommended customer guidance to send right away:
1) patch pager config: set concurrency to 1-2 and add per-page jittered backoff.
2) set the SDK option to respect server Retry-After for 429s (we should provide the exact flag or patch).
3) if possible, switch to cursor pagination with explicit "continue" instead of concurrent page prefetching.
4) short-term workaround: reduce retry attempts for paginated flows (e.g., max_retries=2) and add exponential backoff with jitter.

Maya: suggested backoff snippet to share with customer: 
```
// simple exp backoff with full jitter
function nextDelay(attempt){
  const base = 200; // ms
  const cap = 10000; // ms
  const raw = Math.min(cap, base * Math.pow(2, attempt));
  return Math.floor(Math.random() * raw); // full jitter
}
```

Liam (SDK): also remind them: for non-idempotent POST endpoints use an idempotency-key. For paginated fetches POST shouldn't be used for retrieving pages; if they are using POST-as-fetch then idempotency-key + server-side dedupe solves duplicate-side effects but not rate amplification.

Jen (SRE): operational guidance for us: consider adding a short-lived global backoff signal to SDKs (server can return a header like X-Global-Backoff=60 to request clients back off for a short window). We already have per-account rate metadata but not a coordinated client signal. This would help mitigate immediate retry storms.

Jordan: repro steps I collected from customer to attach to the ticket: 
1) run their pager with concurrency=4 against /v1/objects with a large dataset.
2) introduce a transient delay on the server for one page to force a 429 on that page.
3) observe concurrent page fetches retrying and causing >80% bucket utilization and persistent 429s.

Maya: I'll draft the customer note with the recommended pager config and the backoff snippet. Liam — can you open a small SDK PR to add a pager flag (no-auto-retry) and to respect Retry-After consistently? Jen — can you add an internal follow-up to evaluate a global-backoff header?

Liam (SDK): will open PR today and add docs for pagination best-practices.

Jen (SRE): will file the internal ops ticket, include a quick rollback/mitigation plan for high-volume customers.

Jordan: thanks team — I'll update the support ticket and send the patch instructions to the customer. :thumbsup:
